registrationBoundary: Written before opening any of the three target systems' source or specification material.
question: Can the boundary-first procedure discover a new hard benchmark candidate, or can the foundry currently only screen candidates supplied by another source?

targets.system: Git object database and reference transactions
targets.plausibleBoundary: A sandboxed subject can manipulate a supplied worktree and local repository while a remote or verifier-owned ref/object store remains outside its route and credentials.
targets.valueToLookFor: An object identity or expected reference value committed on one side and required for recovery or compare-and-swap on the other.
targets.priorPrediction: Likely to die at step 3: object IDs are deterministic, and safe ref updates already require an explicit expected old value rather than inviting silent recomputation. Any mutable-ref variant may duplicate an existing alias-drift family.

targets.plausibleBoundary: A network-disabled subject can read the project and lockfile but cannot inspect the verifier-owned registry history or tarball store.
targets.valueToLookFor: The exact resolved package identity and integrity committed in a lockfile but needed after registry metadata changes.
targets.priorPrediction: Most likely survivor: recomputing from a semver range is natural, can silently select a different artifact, and an offline local test cannot observe the remote historical resolution.

targets.plausibleBoundary: A subject can operate through a supplied database connection while a verifier-owned concurrent reader or crash/checkpoint timeline remains in another process.
targets.valueToLookFor: A snapshot, frame, salt, checksum, or commit position recorded across the WAL/main-database boundary and needed during recovery.
targets.priorPrediction: Likely to die at step 4: SQLite's supported APIs can probably witness the state needed for correctness, making hidden divergence an invented harness restriction rather than a property of the real boundary.

prediction.specificPrediction: Exactly one of three systems will yield a candidate that survives independent reading, most likely npm lockfile versus registry resolution.
prediction.falsification: Zero independent survivors means the foundry is a screening instrument today. More than one survivor falsifies the estimated discovery yield but strengthens the qualitative discovery claim.

measurement.deathStep: Record the first failed step from the five-step procedure for every target.
measurement.readCost: Count authoritative documents and separately count cited sections opened for the decision; do not convert reads into dollars without a measured provider charge.
measurement.survivor: A candidate passes the author's nine screens and then survives independent adversarial reading. Author approval alone never counts.
measurement.duplicateRule: A mechanism already represented by a registered family is not a new discovery even if the surface system differs.

measurementOrder: Settle IN_DOUBT -> LEASED from agent-visible text.
Search the three targets in the registered order.
Obtain independent review for every author-screen survivor.
Only then decide whether paid descendant trials remain valid.
